program: Emergency housing and critical-needs assistance, with food-bank grants

nutshell.headline: Credible housing prevention; uncertain health conversion
nutshell.body: The modeled housing-health component of a $10,000 whole gift yields 0.01326 expected Bay QALYs, or $7,541,069 per10. This is not measured health impact or a complete estimate of food-related benefits.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Timely assistance can avert some homelessness; a Santa Clara randomized trial supports the causal housing pathway.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: Prevented homelessness is not a QALY. Finite health benefits and funding response are judgments;96.3% of expected health comes from the favorable world.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: HOLD giving recommendation. Independently audited for exploratory publication; current marginal capacity and the unquantified food-health contribution remain unresolved.

programSection.body: EIN94-3019992, formerly Chronicle Season of Sharing Fund. Nine Bay counties use coordinating agencies and fiscal agents to pay landlords, utilities and other vendors. Gifts also support food banks.

steps.title: Charge whole operations
steps.detail: Keep sponsor-funded administration, fundraising, agent/county fees and food-bank allocations in whole expense; the100%-to-help claim is not zero overhead.

steps.title: Deliver assistance beyond funded baseline
steps.detail: Model cash additionality for reserves, other donors/public sources and partner capacity. Convert the housing/family pool into grant equivalents, not observed unique households.

steps.title: Convert only incremental housing to finite health
steps.detail: Absolute risk difference × transfer × effective affected persons × utility × avoided duration; independently subtract harms.

programSection.boundary: No food-bank meal-to-QALY credit, no duplicated food recipient benefits. Food health is omitted, not asserted zero. Full societal costs of partnercasework/volunteering remain incomplete. No lifetime, mortality, income or fiscal-savings credit.

model.headline: Whole-gift housing-health model
model.body: Nearly5000families is an approximate activity statement.4482is months of rent, not unique families. The model uses housing/family dollars divided by an assumed grant size with dedup and housing relevance; no unsupported exact annual patient denominator.

equation.label: Net Bay housing health
equation.expression: gift/whole expense × ((family/housing pool − provider grants)/assumed grant × dedup) × cash additionality × [housing relevance × .038 × transfer × persons × utility × years − harmQ] × Bay share

inputs.label: Grant-equivalent denominator
inputs.basis: $11,179,746 family/housing cash; $2,000–$3,500 assumed grant and90–98%dedup. Not observed distinct households.

inputs.label: Housing-relevant share
inputs.basis: Pool includes critical needs; not every grant prevents homelessness.

inputs.label: Gift-created assistance
inputs.basis: Reserves and partner/publicfunding are alternatives; no dated incremental tranche.

inputs.label: Six-month homelessness risk difference
inputs.basis: Adjusted ITT, not relative reduction or mortality. Favorable transfer>1 is an explicit high-risk extrapolation.

inputs.label: Persons × utility × incremental years
inputs.basis: All analystjudgments; effective health-person equivalents are not measuredhouseholdsize. Duration ends with alternativehousing/convergence. Recorded homeless-days provide a narrower empirical anchor:2.5days avoided peroffer at6months versus6.94days implied by .038×.5years before transfer. Health persistence beyond recorded homelessness is unverified.

inputs.label: Independent harmQ per delivered grant
inputs.basis: Potential delayed alternativecare, misallocation or instability; not measured adverseevents.

inputs.label: Bay health share
inputs.basis: Nine-county program; exact residence at healthbenefit time unavailable.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Subjective weights fixed before execution. No world currently below$1M/10 for quantifiedhousinghealth; this does not establish a zero probability in reality, especially with omittedfoodbenefits.
model.fundingBoundary: FY2025 cash$5.305M, unrestrictednetassets$5.233M andrestricted$2.664M. Sponsors pay supportingexpenses. These are fundedbaseline, not proof of eitherzero or unlimited room. Some county/agent fees included; other complementary public/partnercosts unknown.

evidence.population: At-risk applicants, not all nine-county grantrecipients
evidence.result: Six-month adjusted ITT reduction3.8percentagepoints from4.1%control homelessness; rawtreatment0.9%.
evidence.transfer: Administrative homelessness outcome, not measuredQALY. Grantrecipient effect is not automatically ITT; usingofferanchor with transfer is explicit conservative convention.

evidence.result: Rentpayment/eviction-concern benefits with suggestive self-reportedhealth effects.
evidence.transfer: Does not establish the model’sutility orduration. No symptom-score-to-QALY mapping invented.

evidence.result: Supportcosts real despite sponsors covering them; foodandhousing grants distinct.
evidence.transfer: No program-only or netfiscal-savings headline. Partner service costs incomplete.

evidence.design: Santa Clara trial Table2 and TableA6; independent source audit
evidence.population: 578 pre-March2020 applicants; not the full pandemic sample
evidence.result: The .038 estimate is agency-month-strata-adjusted ITT. Effects were absent during the pandemic and stronger without children. Table2 reports 2.5 fewer recorded homeless-days at6months and7.5 at12months; covariate-adjusted TableA6 estimates are1.9 and5.7days.
evidence.transfer: The untransferred .038 risk reduction × .5year assumption implies6.94days peroffer, exceeding the six-month2.5day estimate. Broader unrecorded health duration could differ, but is not established. These empirical duration anchors do not validate the assumed utility or household multiplier; coefficients unchanged.

reservations: Health conversion is much weaker than housing prevention evidence.
Grant size, unique-recipient dedup and housing-specific allocation are priors; historical rent-month and family counts do not resolve them.
Foodhealth omitted; this quantifiedhousingcomponent is not a complete whole-org health valuation.
Favorable high-risk transfer and householdhealth multiplier dominate expectation.
No proven marginal funding tranche or guarantee of100000dollar scaling.
Same public/partner outcomes must not also be credited in full to recipient agencies or foodbanks.
excludedBenefits: Food-relatedhealth remains unquantified; no mealcount conversion.
No long-run mortality, childdevelopment, income, legal or crime benefit added.
No avoided shelter/health-systemcosts subtracted from donatedcash.
